README — ZMongo Video Demo
widgets_values:
# ZMongo Video Demo: Save, Retrieve, and Reuse Media

This workflow teaches a complete ZMongo media loop:

1. Connect to your Business Process Applications / ZMongo account.
2. Save a start image into the `images` collection.
3. Browse collections, documents, and flattened field paths.
4. Store or retrieve prompt/metadata values using dot-path fields.
5. Load the saved image back from ZMongo.
6. Generate a short image-to-video clip.
7. Save the resulting video frames to ZMongo and rebuild an MP4 from those frames.

## Before running

- Enter your `username` and `zai_api_key` in **1. Connect to ZMongo**.
- Keep `base_url` as `https://businessprocessapplications.com` unless testing a local backend.
- Use `images` for saved start images.
- Use `image_data` for the image field path.
- Use `image_sequences` for saved video frame sequences.

## Teaching goal

New users should understand that ZMongo is not just a save button. It lets ComfyUI workflows store media, retrieve it by document id, inspect flattened paths, and reuse stored values in later workflow steps.

nodes.title: Instructions — Connect
widgets_values:
# Step 1 — Connect

Use **1. Connect to ZMongo**.

Required fields:

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://businessprocessapplications.com` |
| `username` | Your BPA/ZMongo username |
| `zai_api_key` | Your API key from the account page |
| `comfy_zmongo_prefix` | `/comfy-zmongo` |

After the node runs, the status should confirm that the session is valid. If authentication fails, open the ZMongo panel, login or register, then copy a fresh API key into this node.

The workflow has been sanitized: no private API key or username is stored in this demo file.

nodes.title: Instructions — Save / Reload Image
widgets_values:
# Step 2 — Save and reload an image

This section demonstrates the core ZMongo image loop.

## Save

The **Save Start Image to ZMongo** node writes an image to:

```text
collection: images
field_path: image_data
filename: zmongo_video_demo_start_image.png
```

When `document_id` is blank, ZMongo creates a new document. The returned `document_id` is the record you will use later.

## Reload

The **Load Start Image from ZMongo** node uses:

```text
collection_name + document_id + field_path
```

to retrieve the image. The preview node confirms that the saved image can be loaded back into ComfyUI.

This is the key teaching point: once an image is in ZMongo, later workflows can reuse it without manually browsing files.

nodes.title: Instructions — Browse ZMongo
widgets_values:
# Step 3 — Browse records and fields

Use these nodes to teach how ZMongo documents are structured.

1. **List Collections** shows available collections.
2. **Select Collection** picks one collection by index.
3. **List Documents in Collection** returns document ids.
4. **Select Document ID** picks one document id.
5. **List Flattened Field Paths** exposes dot-path keys such as:

```text
image_data
prompt.positive
prompt.negative
metadata.demo
```

Flattened paths are important because ZMongo nodes can save or retrieve deeply nested values by a simple string path.

nodes.title: Instructions — Save / Get Values
widgets_values:
# Step 4 — Save and verify prompt/metadata values

This section teaches saving normal text or JSON values into a document.

Recommended demo field:

```text
prompt.positive
```

Recommended value:

```text
A friendly robot slowly walks through a glowing futuristic garden...
```

The **Save Prompt / Metadata Value** node writes the value. The **Get Saved Prompt / Metadata Value** node reads the same field back so users can verify the save worked.

Use this pattern for prompts, negative prompts, model notes, project metadata, workflow status, captions, tags, and review notes.

nodes.title: Instructions — Image to Video
widgets_values:
# Step 5 — Generate video from a stored image

This section uses the image reloaded from ZMongo as the start image for the video generator.

The subgraph is configured as an image-to-video demo. For a first teaching run, keep the settings small:

| Setting | Beginner value |
|---|---:|
| Width | 640 |
| Height | 640 |
| Length | 81 frames |
| FPS | 16 |

Video generation can be VRAM-heavy. If the workflow fails with out-of-memory errors, reduce width, height, or frame length before changing model files.

nodes.title: Instructions — Save / Rebuild Video Frames
widgets_values:
# Step 6 — Save video frames and rebuild the video

This section teaches video persistence.

1. **GetVideoComponents** extracts frames from the generated video.
2. **Save Video Frames to ZMongo** stores each frame in the `image_sequences` collection.
3. **Load Video Frames from ZMongo** retrieves the stored frame sequence.
4. **Create MP4 from Loaded Frames** rebuilds a video from the retrieved frames.
5. **Save Teaching Demo Video** writes the final MP4 to ComfyUI output.

Recommended sequence settings:

```text
collection: image_sequences
image_prefix: zmongo_video_demo_frame
start_frame_number: 0
```

This demonstrates a practical production pattern: generate once, store frames, reload later, and rebuild or continue processing.

nodes.title: Troubleshooting
widgets_values:
# Troubleshooting

## Authentication fails

- Confirm username and API key.
- Confirm `base_url` is correct.
- Confirm `comfy_zmongo_prefix` is `/comfy-zmongo`.

## Image does not reload

Check:

```text
collection_name = images
field_path = image_data
document_id = the id returned by the save node
```

## Field path save fails

Use writable paths such as:

```text
prompt.positive
prompt.negative
metadata.note
metadata.review_status
```

Do not save to protected identity fields such as `_id`.

## Video generation is too slow or runs out of VRAM

Reduce:

```text
width
height
length
```

Then run the workflow again. Start small for teaching and increase quality only after the full ZMongo loop works.

nodes.title: VRAM Guidance
widgets_values:
# VRAM guidance

This video section can be demanding.

Beginner-safe approach:

| Setting | Suggested starting point |
|---|---:|
| Width | 640 |
| Height | 640 |
| Length | 81 frames |
| FPS | 16 |

If you hit out-of-memory errors, reduce `width`, `height`, or `length` first. Do not start debugging ZMongo until the video generator itself runs successfully.

nodes.title: Model Files Required
widgets_values:
# Required Wan 2.2 model files

Place the model files in the matching ComfyUI model folders before running the video section.

## Diffusion models

```text
ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/
  wan2.2_i2v_high_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors
  wan2.2_i2v_low_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors
```

## LoRAs

```text
ComfyUI/models/loras/
  wan2.2_i2v_lightx2v_4steps_lora_v1_high_noise.safetensors
  wan2.2_i2v_lightx2v_4steps_lora_v1_low_noise.safetensors
```

## Text encoder and VAE

```text
ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/
  umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors

ComfyUI/models/vae/
  wan_2.1_vae.safetensors
```

The demo uses the 4-step LoRA path because it is easier for new users to test quickly.

nodes.title: About the 4-Step LoRA
widgets_values: The LightX2V 4-step LoRA reduces generation time and is better for a teaching workflow. It may reduce motion/detail quality compared with a full-step generation.
